# Beyond the three-year plan: Building cold chains that adapt as fast as conditions change


November 17, 2026


Share This Article


[Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/beyond-three-year-plan&title=Beyond%20the%20three-year%20plan:%20Building%20cold%20chains%20that%20adapt%20as%20fast%20as%20conditions%20change)[LinkedIn](http://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/beyond-three-year-plan&title=Beyond%20the%20three-year%20plan:%20Building%20cold%20chains%20that%20adapt%20as%20fast%20as%20conditions%20change&source=https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/beyond-three-year-plan)[Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/beyond-three-year-plan&title=Beyond%20the%20three-year%20plan:%20Building%20cold%20chains%20that%20adapt%20as%20fast%20as%20conditions%20change&hashtags=onelineage)


For food producers and manufacturers, planning is essential to keeping products moving, managing costs and meeting customer expectations. Yet geopolitical uncertainty, changing trade policies, evolving consumer demands and operating cost pressures can quickly challenge even the most carefully developed strategies. Businesses therefore need to look beyond long-term forecasts and consider how effectively their supply chains can respond when circumstances change.


This was one of the themes explored during Lineage’s participation in Business Reporter’s SupplyChainTalk, “Faster decisions for a more resilient frozen food supply chain”. Raul Fores, Lineage’s Regional Vice President of Spain, France, Belgium and Italy, joined Cyrille Filott of Rabobank and Chris Fielden of GLACIER Global, in a discussion hosted by Ana Maria Velica. The panel explored how food businesses can respond to uncertainty through faster decisions, innovation, automation, real-time visibility, strategic partnerships and more flexible operating models.


## Make flexibility part of the network


Efficiency is the key to managing costs, maintaining service and protecting product quality in the supply chain. But building a network around expected volumes or stable operating conditions can leave businesses open to issues when unplanned disruptions arise. Fluctuating harvests, increased customer demands and changing transportation requirements mean food businesses need to be able to quickly adapt to stay ahead. Success often depends on it.


For temperature-sensitive products, being ready for change is essential. Storage and transportation need to maintain appropriate temperature conditions, while unexpected volume changes or delays can put pressure on available capacity and planned movements. Access to[strategically located cold storage](https://www.onelineage.com/services/global-warehousing) ,[suitable transportation options](https://www.onelineage.com/services/global-integrated-solutions) and a connected network of facilities can give businesses more alternatives when their original plans need to be adjusted.


## Faster decisions start with better information


A flexible network is most effective when the people managing it have access to relevant, timely information. When inventory, order and shipment tracking is fragmented across multiple systems or partners, identifying constraints, assessing alternatives and coordinating a response becomes more challenging. Better visibility across an integrated supply chain helps connect planning with day-to-day execution. This gives teams a clearer understanding of what is happening across their operations and supports decisions based on current conditions rather than relying solely on earlier assumptions.


[Technology](https://www.onelineage.com/about-us/innovation-technology) plays an important role in making this possible. Automation, AI and real-time visibility offer opportunities to improve information flows, support analysis and streamline workflows, but their value depends on how effectively they address operational needs.


At Lineage, technology is an important part of how we support customers in managing their cold chains.[Lineage Link®](https://www.onelineage.com/lineage-link) provides customers with access to inventory, order and appointment information across participating Lineage facilities, helping them gain visibility to better manage operations and support coordination. Combining these tools with the expertise of our teams can help customers manage their operations as supply chain conditions evolve.


## Resilience is built through partnership


No single facility or technology can address every supply chain challenge. Resilience depends on how well the different parts of a network work together and on the relationships between customers, logistics providers and suppliers. Strong collaboration helps businesses identify changing requirements, discuss potential constraints and coordinate resources across facilities and transportation. This is particularly important in temperature-controlled logistics, where storage, transportation and product handling need to be considered together to support the movement and quality requirements of food products.


[One example of how Lineage works with customers](https://www.onelineage.com/news-stories/growing-without-pains) to address changing requirements involved a frozen produce manufacturer preparing for an anticipated harvest of more than 47 million kilograms. With its existing storage network unable to accommodate the projected volume, the customer worked with Lineage to expand its operation from 3 facilities to 15 in a matter of weeks, accommodating 64,000 pallets of frozen produce. By bringing together additional facilities and coordinating operations across the network, Lineage helped the customer manage a significant seasonal increase in volume while supporting its changing storage needs.


Every customer’s requirements are different. At Lineage, we connect[temperature-controlled warehousing](https://www.onelineage.com/services/cold-storage-warehousing) , transportation, technology and supply chain expertise to develop solutions around each customer’s products and business objectives.


## Build for what comes next


Long-term planning remains important, but it needs to be adaptable and informed by changing business conditions. Food businesses should regularly consider where their networks have limited alternatives, how quickly alternative capacity could be assessed, whether teams have the information they need to make timely decisions and how effectively logistics partners can coordinate activity across facilities and transportation. Asking these questions can help organisations identify opportunities to improve their flexibility and prepare for changing conditions.


The strongest cold chains aren’t built on the assumption that every forecast will prove correct. They are those designed with the ability to respond when actual conditions differ from expectations, while continuing to focus on product quality, operational requirements and customer needs.


At Lineage, we work alongside customers to understand the challenges they face and explore how connected temperature-controlled warehousing, transportation, technology and operational expertise can support their supply chains. By bringing these capabilities together, we aim to help food businesses navigate complexity, adapt to changes and prepare for what comes next.
